messages:
alex: FYI I landed the paged-attention kernel switch yesterday and we see a consistent ~12-18% tail-latency regression on small-batch decode workloads (batch_size <= 4). reproduces locally on a single A100 and in perf-runner.
maria: ugh. is that for prefill or decode or both?
alex: decode only. prefill numbers look neutral or slightly better. seems tied to KV cache hits (i.e., continuing sequences).

jin: can you paste the benchmark run and profiler snapshot? are we seeing lower SM occupancy or more global memory stalls?
alex: benchmark snippet below (from perf-runner, 2k steps warm, 1k measured):

```
model: redwood-mini-7b
hw: a100-40g
mode: decode
batch_sizes: [1,2,4]
kernels: paged-attn (current), flash2, fused-attn
results (p50/p95/ms):
  paged-attn: 12.4 / 34.7 (b1), 13.0 / 36.5 (b2), 15.2 / 41.3 (b4)
  fused-attn: 11.0 / 29.5 (b1), 11.6 / 30.2 (b2), 12.8 / 32.0 (b4)
  flash2: 11.4 / 30.1 (b1), 11.9 / 30.8 (b2), 13.5 / 33.9 (b4)
notes: paged-attn regresses mostly at p95 and higher, especially for b2/b4.
```

maria: that p95 gap is concerning. perf-bot, did the CI nightly compare flag this?
perf-bot: nightly-regressions: flag=red
  commit: a3d9f7
  test: decode-small-batch
  delta_p95: +15.2% (paged-attn vs baseline fused-attn)
  artifacts: https://perf.internal/reports/1791122334

jin: I profiled with Nsight and there's a notable increase in L2 traffic and lower warp efficiency for the paged variant during KV loads. Looks like the paged scatter/gather pattern isn't coalescing when KV pages are hot, causing extra global memory ops.

alex: stack trace from nvprof:
```
GPU activities:
  kernel 1: paged_attn_forward - avg sm_efficiency 53%, achieved_occupancy 0.43
  kernel 2: kv_read_pages - memory_throughput 120 GB/s
  kernel 3: softmax_fused - sm_efficiency 66%
```

jin: contrast with fused-attn: sm_efficiency ~78-82% and lower memory throughput spikes. That matches why fused wins for small decode where KV accesses are frequent and sequence lengths are short.

taylor: might be a kernel-selection heuristic bug: we currently pick paged-attn if "estimated_prefill_mem > threshold" without considering runtime kv_hit_rate or decode vs prefill. The selector is too static.

alex: agreed. I sketched a quick runtime heuristic: prefer fused-attn for decode when (batch_size <= 4) OR (kv_hit_rate >= 0.6)

```
# pseudocode for selection (rough)
if mode == "prefill":
  choose paged_attn if seq_len > 1024 else flash2
else: # decode
  if batch_size <= 4 or kv_hit_rate >= 0.6:
    choose fused_attn
  else:
    choose paged_attn
```

sam: that seems reasonable but watch out: fused-attn can regress prefill throughput on long sequences. need to gate selection to avoid hurting large prefill jobs.

maria: could we instead add a micro-benchmark at session start: run a tiny probe (1-2 iterations) that measures an on-device kv_load pattern and picks the kernel accordingly? low risk and runtime-adaptive.

jin: probe is good, but it adds jitter to cold-starts. Maybe cache the probe result per session and expire it after N tokens or T seconds.

alex: implementation plan: 1) quick probe at session init for decode sessions (opt-out via env), 2) selector change with thresholds and cache, 3) rollout as canary (5% decode traffic) + tight monitoring. I'll draft patch.

perf-bot: recommended rollback window if p95 delta > 8% or error-rate delta > 0.1% during canary.

maria: also add an A/B perf test that runs long-running prefill workloads to ensure we don't regress throughput for non-decode.

alex: action items:
- alex: open PR with heuristic + probe + selector unit tests (will include perf-runner task)
- jin: validate Nsight traces for fused vs paged across more layers and provide list of layer shapes where paged loses
- taylor: add canary config and alert thresholds in console deployments
- sam: coordinate rollout timing with infra so we can shrink canary quickly if needed

sam: thanks. if we can get that PR today I can start a canary tomorrow.

alex: pulling together PR now, will ping when ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: thanks all. this thread saved us a nasty surprise for customers.

perf-bot: note: recorded bench artifacts and Nsight captures are at https://perf.internal/artifacts/1791122334 (expires in 30d)
